# Generator stage configs generated by cmsDriver, with GenPartAnalyzer plots per stage

The four hand-copied configs step1_GEN_ME_cfg.py, step1_GEN_ME_PS_cfg.py, step1_GEN_ME_PS_MPI_cfg.py
and step1_GEN_ME_PS_MPI_Had_cfg.py differed from step1_GEN_cfg.py only in the output file name and the four
Pythia switches PartonLevel:ISR, PartonLevel:FSR, PartonLevel:MPI and HadronLevel:all. They are now produced
by cmsDriver.py, so nothing is edited by hand any more.

- Journey/test/runCMSDrivers_mc2024_BBbar_GEN.sh: GEN-only companion of runCMSDrivers_mc2024_BBbar.sh.
  Same fragment, conditions, era, geometry, beamspot, com energy, fragment symlink and DUMP options as step 1
  of the main script. Five stages: ME, ME_PS, ME_PS_MPI, ME_PS_MPI_Had (HadronLevel:Hadronize on,
  HadronLevel:Decay off) and ME_PS_MPI_Had_Decay (the full event). For each stage it calls cmsDriver.py with
  --customise_commands that set the com energy and append PhaseSpace:pTHatMin (PTHATMIN, default 100 GeV,
  overriding the 30 GeV of the fragment) and the Pythia level switches to processParameters, runs cmsRun,
  and then runs GenPartAnalyzer on the output. Everything goes to the output directory (OUTDIR, default GEN/ below the current directory):
  step1_GEN_<stage>_cfg.py, step1_GEN_<stage>_cfg.driver.log, step1_GEN_<stage>_out.root,
  step1_GEN_<stage>_out.log, genPartAnalyzer_<stage>_out.pdf, genPartAnalyzer_<stage>_out.root and
  genPartAnalyzer_<stage>_out.log. The plugin library is rebuilt when it is older than the plugin sources.

    ./runCMSDrivers_mc2024_BBbar_GEN.sh                      # all five stages, 1000 events each
    EVENTS=200 STAGES="ME ME_PS" ./runCMSDrivers_mc2024_BBbar_GEN.sh
    RUN=0 ./runCMSDrivers_mc2024_BBbar_GEN.sh                # only generate the configs
    ANALYZE=0 ...                                            # skip GenPartAnalyzer
    ANALYZE_EVENTS=3 ...                                     # events drawn per stage (default 1)

- Journey/plugins/GenPartAnalyzer.cc: three new parameters. pdfFile collects all plots as pages of one PDF
  (opened on the first page, closed in endJob) instead of one PDF per stage and event. maxStage limits the
  generator-record stages that are analysed and drawn, so a sample generated with later Pythia levels off
  gets only the pages that exist: ME 1 page, ME_PS 2, ME_PS_MPI 3, ME_PS_MPI_Had 4, ME_PS_MPI_Had_Decay 5
  (per analysed event;
  pages are grouped by event). sampleLabel is printed in the right panel above the legend, '|' separates
  lines; the stages list on the right greys out the stages beyond maxStage.
- Journey/test/genPartAnalyzer_cfg.py: exposes maxStage, pdfFile and sampleLabel as VarParsing options and
  clears the VarParsing output-name tags, which otherwise append _numEvent<N> to outputFile when maxEvents > 0.

Bug found in the hand-copied files: they missed the comma after 'PhaseSpace:pTHatMin = 100. ', so Python
joined it with the next literal into 'PhaseSpace:pTHatMin = 100. PartonLevel:ISR = off'. Pythia read the
value 100. and silently dropped the rest, so PartonLevel:ISR was never set and stayed on in all four earlier
runs (their logs show no PartonLevel:ISR line in the Pythia settings table). The generated configs do not have
this problem: a 3-event run of each stage shows exactly the intended switches in the settings table, and the
analyzer logs show 2 particles alive at the hard-process stage, 7 after the shower, 145 after MPI and
579 status-1 particles after hadronisation and decays for the first event.
